catalog_citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. & Lama Ziwo. 1999. Laghuu or Xá Phó, a new language of the Yi group. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 22.1: 1-10.
catalog_locator: p. 5 sec. 2.5 'Tones' (page scan viewed); p. 3 sec. 2.0; p. 8-9 (scanned of same scan)
catalog_quote: [p.3] One obvious feature of Laghuu is the word structure. While individual Laghuu morphemes are monosyllabic, words are typically disyllabic compounds, as in the other Yi languages. The syllable may be analyzed into an initial, a rhyme, and a tone. ... [p.5] 2.5. Tones. There are five tones in Laghuu. See Figure 2. This language does not appear to have noticeable tense/lax voice quality contrast. ... [p.8-9] There are five distinctive tones in this language (see Figure 2). There is also a tone sandhi phenomenon where 21 becomes 24, before another syllable with a 33 tone ... A 55 tone often develops a falling component at the end of a word, becoming 54 or 53.

sources.quote: p.313: 'Xa Pho has only one rising tone with the value 24. The other tones have the shapes 54, 44, 33, and 21.' p.313 sec. 4.2: a second location (Son La) 'The tonal system appears to be identical to Lao Cai'. Initials, rhymes, nasal codas, velar+lateral clusters described; no mention of stress, accent, or syllable prominence anywhere in the chapter's Xa Pho section (a full-text search for stress/accent full text for stress/accent/iamb/sesquisyllabic: only hits are in the Phu Kha section? none for Xa Pho).
sources.locator: sec. 4 'Xa Pho, Laghuu, or Phu La Lao', pp. 312-313 (sec. 4.1-4.2)
sources.note: Catalog (from Edmondson & Lama 1999) codes lexical tone, five tones 55/44/33/21/24, no tense/lax contrast. This paper gives the same five-tone system with the high tone written 54 instead of 55 (24, 54, 44, 33, 21), consistent with the catalog's own remark that word-final 55 often becomes 54/53; adds a second datapoint (Son La) with an identical tonal system. No pitch plots for Xa Pho; no statement on stress, accent or weight. First-hand: 'we rely largely on data collected from Mr. Ma A Suan of Nam Sang Commune, Sa Pa District' (p. 312).
